skill.name: commit-drafter
skill.description: Drafts commit messages by collecting staged Git changes and preparing structured context for AI review.
skill.summary: Draft commit messages from staged Git status and diff context.
skill.author: abereyes

security_audit.summary: Both static findings were adjudicated as false positives. drafter.py uses subprocess.run for fixed git commands without shell execution, and SKILL.md contains markdown backticks only. No evidence found of prompt injection text, data exfiltration intent, network calls, or malicious behavior.

static_findings.snippet: No more staring at `git diff` trying to write a commit message. No more useless templates with [TODO

finding_verdicts.reason: subprocess.run executes git with an argument list, no shell, and a timeout. The command values are fixed internal git subcommands, so no command injection path is evident.
The backticks on line 55 are markdown formatting around git diff in prose. They are not executable code and do not invoke a shell.

content.user_title: Draft Git Commit Messages From Staged Changes
content.value_statement: Writing commit messages from staged changes takes time and can miss important context. This skill collects git status and diff details so AI can draft a clear message.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether the current directory is a Git repository.
Detects staged added, modified, deleted, and renamed files.
Summarizes per-file insertions and deletions from staged diff statistics.
Includes full staged diff content for AI review.
Produces commit-message instructions with summary and What, Why, and How sections.
limitations: Requires a local Git repository with staged changes.
Does not create commits or modify repository files.
May include sensitive staged diff content in the AI context.
Does not validate whether the final message follows project conventions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a focused commit message
use_cases.description: Generate a clear draft after staging one logical change set.

use_cases.title: Standardize team commit summaries
use_cases.description: Use staged diff context to draft messages with consistent structure.

use_cases.title: Review contribution changes quickly
use_cases.description: Create a readable draft before final review of staged open source changes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Commit Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a commit message for my staged changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this after staging a simple change.

prompt_templates.title: Concise Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a commit message for my staged changes with a concise summary line.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when your project prefers short commit titles.

prompt_templates.title: Structured Explanation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a commit message with What, Why, and How sections for the staged changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for changes that need reviewer context.

prompt_templates.title: Review Before Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the staged diff context, draft a commit message, and note any issues I should check before committing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before committing larger or riskier changes.

output_examples.input: User asks for a draft after staging authentication test updates.
output_examples.output:
Update authentication tests

What: Add coverage for expired sessions.
Why: Prevent regressions in login behavior.
How: Add assertions for redirects and error handling.

output_examples.input: User asks for a draft after staging documentation edits.
output_examples.output:
Improve setup documentation

What: Clarify installation steps and configuration notes.
Why: Help new contributors start faster.
How: Reorder instructions and add missing context.

output_examples.input: User asks for a draft after staging a small bug fix.
output_examples.output:
Fix profile save error

What: Handle missing display names during profile updates.
Why: Avoid failed saves for existing accounts.
How: Apply a fallback value before validation.

best_practices: Stage only files that belong in one logical commit.
Review the drafted message before committing.
Remove secrets from staged changes before using AI review.
anti_patterns: Do not use one draft for unrelated changes.
Do not accept generated messages without checking accuracy.
Do not stage secret files before drafting a message.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: No. It prints context and instructions. You choose the final commit message.

faq.question: Does it require staged changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks staged files and returns an error when nothing is staged.

faq.question: Which Git data does it inspect?
faq.answer: It reads status, staged diff statistics, and the full staged diff.

faq.question: Can it handle renamed files?
faq.answer: Yes. It categorizes renamed files along with added, modified, and deleted files.

faq.question: Will it follow my project commit style?
faq.answer: It provides a structured draft. You should edit the message for project-specific rules.

faq.question: Can staged secrets appear in the output?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes full staged diff content, so review staged files first.
